{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink / Mortgage Logic.com Hosting, Licence and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Client / Mortgage Logic.com)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — issues, redlines and negotiation posture

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is workable, but the risk allocation is markedly one-sided in TrueLink's favour on the three items we treat as critical: indemnity, IP/data ownership and limitation of liability. TrueLink's indemnity (§ 12.b) is confined to its own breach of the Agreement, with no third-party IP infringement, breach-of-law, unauthorised-disclosure or gross-negligence cover, while § 12.a imposes a very broad indemnity on us. The only liability cap protects TrueLink alone, leaving our liability wholly uncapped, with no mutual consequential-damages exclusion and no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnity, fraud or IP infringement. On ownership, § 2(d) confirms TrueLink keeps the Interface (acceptable), but there is no counterpart clause giving us ownership of Support Services work product or confirming we retain rights in Client Content, our marks and borrower Credit Data — and § 8(d) grants TrueLink a broad worldwide right to use, license, resell and exploit Credit Data with no ownership reservation.

A second tier of high-severity items constrains our commercial freedom and exit: a requirements-style exclusivity obliging us to order a TrueLink credit report for every borrower (§ 3(i)); a licence grant running to "Client" only, excluding affiliates and contractors; an assignment clause with no successor/M&A carve-out, no reasonableness standard and no bar on assignment to our competitors (§ 15); and no express termination-for-convenience right, with TrueLink able to exit at renewal on only 30 days' notice against the 60-day migration burden it places on us (§§ 13–14). We have also flagged the absence of transition assistance and data return/deletion obligations, the absence of any performance warranty beyond Y2K (§ 9), an open-ended take-or-pay minimum monthly fee (§ 5(a)) with dispute rights stripped by § 6, uncapped renewal pricing after the one-year freeze, and the absence of any insurance covenant.

Several areas are clean and require no redline: no audit rights against us, no non-compete, no employee non-solicit, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, an MFN that runs in our favour (§ 6), and a mutual California law/San Luis Obispo County venue clause with no arbitration, which sits within our accepted fallback range. Note that findings in this memo were generated from the playbook review and were not independently re-verified.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | TrueLink indemnity limited to its own breach; no third-party IP, breach-of-law, unauthorised-disclosure or gross negligence/wilful misconduct cover. Expanded § 12.b and added notice/control/cooperation procedure. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 2 LICENSE | No ownership of Support Services work product, Client Content/IP or borrower data; § 8(d) grants broad Credit Data exploitation rights without reserving ownership. Added ownership clause after § 2(d) with licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP and no joint ownership. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | Cap protects TrueLink only; our liability uncapped; narrow "compensation paid" basis, no consequential-damages exclusion, no carve-outs. Redlined to mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential exclusion, and Excluded Claims uncapped. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 15) | No successor/M&A carve-out for Client, unqualified consent standard, no bar on assignment to our competitors. Added carve-out, reasonableness standard, competitor bar and confirmation that a Client ownership change is not a deemed assignment. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE (§ 3(i)) | Requirements-style obligation to source a TrueLink credit report for every borrower, with no volume, term or performance exit. Made the ordering right permissive and confirmed non-exclusivity. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE | Grant runs to "Client" only — affiliates and contractors excluded; § 15 permits consent-free transfer only to a financially responsible affiliate. Added affiliates/contractors and a successor-transfer carve-out. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY (§§ 13–14) | Client exit only implied, notice period uncertain (up to ~60 days), no prepaid-fee refund; TrueLink may exit at renewal on 30 days' notice. Made our 30-day right and refund express, barred TrueLink mid-term convenience exit, extended TrueLink non-renewal notice to 90 days. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No liquidated damages, penalty, late fee or exit charge payable by us; the § 5(a) monthly floor is a pricing minimum, not stipulated damages. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on us; § 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services. Review the separate Non-Competition Agreement referenced in § 8(d) to confirm it imposes no restraint on us. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitment | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION | § 5(a) imposes a take-or-pay monthly floor (amounts blank) recurring through indefinite auto-renewals, and § 6 strips our documentation and dispute rights for those minimum fees. Deleted the floor and related carve-outs. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 13) | 12-month renewals with mutual 30-day notice are acceptable, but there is no renewal reminder and no cap on renewal uplift once the § 6 one-year freeze expires. Added 60-day reminder and capped increases at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 14) | No obligation on TrueLink to return, export or delete our data or to assist migration; § 13 places the entire exit burden on us. Inserted transition assistance, data return and certified deletion into § 14 (which survives under § 24). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Missing | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT (§ 9) | Only TrueLink warranty is Y2K; no workmanlike/conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty and no remedy — effectively AS IS. Added conformance warranty with repair/replace/refund in § 9. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No audit, inspection or records-examination right against us; §§ 5–6 run in our favour. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY (§§ 26–27) | Mutual California law, exclusive venue San Luis Obispo County, no arbitration — within our accepted fallback. Accept as drafted. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION (§ 6) | MFN runs in our favour (rates no higher than any other party, plus one-year freeze). No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicit or no-hire binding us. If proposed, we would hold to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to services personnel, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY | No insurance provision despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and processing Client Content and Credit Data. Inserted new § 31 (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request); fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

## Walk-away items

These are the positions we should not concede without escalation:

1. **Vendor IP infringement indemnity (§ 12.b).** We cannot accept a hosted Interface with no defence of third-party IP claims while § 12.a imposes a very broad indemnity on us. TrueLink must also stand behind unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data and its own gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
2. **Mutual cap with carve-outs (§ 12).** A cap that protects TrueLink alone while leaving our liability uncapped is not acceptable. We require mutuality, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and confidentiality, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.
3. **Credit Data ownership (§ 8(d)).** The worldwide right to use, distribute, license, resell and exploit borrower/loan applicant Credit Data cannot stand without an express statement that ownership remains with us and that the § 8(d) licence transfers no ownership.
4. **Requirements exclusivity (§ 3(i)).** An open-ended sole-supplier obligation to buy a TrueLink credit report for every borrower, with no volume, term or performance-based exit, is off-playbook. Fallback: credit reports only, 12 months, terminating on failure to meet the § 3 performance standards.
5. **Data return and deletion on exit (§§ 13–14).** TrueLink holds our Web Site, Client Content and Credit Data on its servers. We must have export in a machine-readable format and certified deletion; an exit regime that makes migration entirely our problem within 60 days is not tenable.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Send the marked-up Agreement with [Playbook] comments, leading on the three critical items (§ 12.b indemnity, § 12 cap, ownership clause after § 2(d)) and the § 8(d) Credit Data ownership reservation.
2. **Sequence the high-severity commercial items.** Table § 3(i) exclusivity, § 2(a) licence scope (affiliates and contractors), § 15 assignment (successor carve-out, reasonableness, competitor bar) and §§ 13–14 termination/non-renewal symmetry as a single package, with the stated fallbacks available.
3. **Complete the blanks and pricing protections.** Obtain the § 5(a) figures from the business team; press deletion of the minimum monthly floor and the § 6 carve-outs, and secure the renewal reminder and CPI/3% uplift cap (5% flat as fallback).
4. **Insert the missing protections.** Transition assistance, data return and certified deletion in § 14; performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund in § 9; new § 31 insurance covenant.
5. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in § 8(d) to confirm it imposes no restraint on us.
6. **Accept and close out the clean items** (audit, governing law and venue, MFN, non-solicit, liquidated damages, non-compete) so we spend negotiating capital only where the playbook requires it."}
